items.title: A fixed yearly fee per legal form, invoiced monthly, is the promise that makes a personal bookkeeper affordable and predictable
items.summary: Kees de Boekhouder prices its service as a fixed yearly subscription per legal form, invoiced monthly and excluding VAT: €840 for an eenmanszaak, €1,140 for a VOF with two partners plus €100 per extra partner, and through the sister company Founders €1,750 for a holding BV and €2,450 for a werkmaatschappij. The fee includes the personal bookkeeper, the app, the quarterly VAT returns, the annual accounts and the income tax return; the FAQ lists add-ons separately (partner income tax return €125 incl. VAT, payroll €17.50 per payslip, bank connection €5 per account per month). The home page frames the sole-proprietor plan as €70 per month.
items.implication: Margin depends on how many clients one bookkeeper can serve well, not on billable hours: every product decision — recognition, matching, review tooling, self-service answers — should be judged by bookkeeper minutes saved per client per year, and plan rules (first full fiscal year, one-month notice afterwards) must be encoded in billing rather than handled by hand.

items.title: Software captures the administration at the source so that the client's effort is a photo, an invoice and a glance at the dashboard
items.summary: The 'wat we doen' page describes the division of labour: the client photographs or uploads receipts and purchase invoices (Scan & Herken recognises them), sends quotes and invoices from the app under one or more trading names, and sees revenue per quarter, cost categories, investments, profit and the VAT to pay or receive on a dashboard that updates as bookings are submitted; the bookkeeper checks the administration, files the quarterly VAT return, prepares the annual accounts and files the income tax return. Documents are stored in the app and deadline reminders are sent.
items.implication: The client app is the intake funnel for the bookkeeper, so recognition quality, categorisation defaults and reminder timing are bookkeeper-productivity features as much as client features; measure 'hours on administration per month' on the client side and 'review turnaround' on the bookkeeper side against the same bookings.

items.title: The Ponto bank connection syncs four times a day and matches automatically, but re-authorisation every 90 to 180 days is a recurring friction
items.summary: The bank connection page explains that Kees connects business bank accounts through Ponto (Isabel Group, a licensed PSD2 provider) to every bank Ponto supports, among them Knab, Rabobank, ABN AMRO and bunq. Transactions are retrieved four times a day and matched automatically against bookings in the administration; what cannot be matched is matched manually or booked directly. The connection costs €5 per month per connected account and the client must re-authorise the consent every 90 to 180 days depending on the bank.
items.implication: Treat consent expiry as a first-class event: predict it per bank, remind the client before the sync stops and show the bookkeeper which clients have a stale connection, because a silent gap in transactions surfaces as missing bookings at quarter-end review; matching precision is the lever that turns €5 add-on revenue into review time saved.

items.title: Roughly 100 people, a large share of them internally trained bookkeepers in three offices, carry the fiscal responsibility for 10,000+ clients
items.summary: The team and vacancy pages present Kees de Boekhouder as a company of roughly 100 people — bookkeepers, marketers, IT and HR — working from offices in Amsterdam, Rotterdam and Utrecht, with bookkeepers trained internally in the company's own method and technology and backed up by colleagues. The home page states that the company has served more than 10,000 entrepreneurs throughout the Netherlands over 15 years; the Head of Growth vacancy confirms the ~100 staff and 10,000 clients and the ambition to grow to 20,000.
items.implication: The number of clients one bookkeeper serves per week is the domain's unit of scale: capacity must be planned per office with backup coverage, internal training must be a product (knowledge base, QA checks), and growth to 20,000 clients must not double the bookkeeper headcount — the workspace, not the hiring plan, has to absorb most of the growth.

items.title: Vortex's 2022 buyout backs a loyal, ambassador-driven client base and the professionalisation of leadership and technology
items.summary: On 24 May 2022 Vortex Capital Partners announced a stake in Kees de Boekhouder, then serving more than 6,500 clients, in a buyout that Accountancy Vanmorgen reported the next day. CEO and co-founder Kees Monteban spoke of solving administrative challenges for entrepreneurs nationwide, and Vortex partner Joost Moerland pointed to the loyal customer base whose clients act as brand ambassadors. Vortex's investment page now reports more than 10,000 clients and a revenue CAGR above 25 percent, and describes its focus as reinforcing leadership, organisational structure and professionalising the technology function, with the ambition to make Kees the go-to brand for bookkeeping services.
items.implication: Retention and referral are the growth engine the investor bought: measure churn and referred-client activation as north-star inputs, keep the personal bookkeeper visible in every scaling decision, and give the professionalised technology function a roadmap that is explicitly about bookkeeper leverage rather than feature parity with software-only tools.

items.title: The growth mandate is 10,000 to 20,000 clients in a market of well over a million freelancers, which requires data-driven segment and channel choices
items.summary: The Top of Minds vacancy for a Head of Growth describes Kees de Boekhouder as a company of about 100 people serving 10,000 clients with the goal of doubling to 20,000, and sizes the addressable market at around 1.4 million freelancers in the Netherlands. CBS counted 1.2 million zzp'ers in 2025 in its narrower definition. The vacancy frames the role around data-driven growth across segments, channels and partnerships.
items.implication: Even at 20,000 clients the company would serve under two percent of Dutch freelancers, so segment focus (creative professions, knowledge workers, starters) and partner channels matter more than mass marketing; instrument the funnel from website request to active client per segment and per channel so that growth budget follows conversion, not volume.

items.title: The zzp population shrank by 62,000 in 2025 while the Belastingdienst enforces the Wet DBA with a soft landing — compliance anxiety is now part of the freelancer's job
items.summary: CBS reported that the number of zzp'ers fell by 62,000 in 2025 to 1.2 million. ZiPconomy's January 2026 analysis explains that the Belastingdienst has enforced the Wet DBA on sham self-employment since 1 January 2025 and that 2026 continues a 'soft landing' in which the approach to enforcement changes in some respects and not in others. Knowledge freelancers working for a few large clients are the group most exposed to reassessment of their status.
items.implication: Position the bookkeeper as the freelancer's compliance ally: keep Wet DBA guidance current in the knowledge base, help clients document their entrepreneurship (multiple clients, own risk, hours criterion), and prepare the path to a BV or to employment for those who leave self-employment, because market contraction makes retention and legal-form transitions more valuable than ever.

items.title: Shrinking deductions and the €20,000 KOR threshold make correct, timely tax advice worth more per euro than ever
items.summary: MKB Servicedesk reports that the zelfstandigenaftrek is reduced to €1,200 in 2026 and will fall further to €900 in 2027, continuing the phased reduction of the self-employed deduction. KVK explains the kleineondernemersregeling (KOR): entrepreneurs with turnover up to €20,000 per year can opt out of VAT obligations, which removes VAT returns but also the right to deduct input VAT. Kees' starters page positions guidance on the VAT number, KOR and startersaftrek as part of the Starters package.
items.implication: The deduction advice a bookkeeper gives is becoming a decision service (KOR yes or no, hours criterion, startersaftrek timing, mkb-winstvrijstelling) rather than a line on the return; encode these rules in the knowledge base with effective dates so every bookkeeper gives the same answer and the app can flag clients near the KOR threshold or the hours criterion before year-end.

items.title: Starters get the same subscription with extra guidance, and their first quarter decides whether they stay
items.summary: The bookkeeper-for-starters page offers new entrepreneurs the same personal-bookkeeper-plus-app subscription as other sole proprietors, with guidance on registering at KVK, obtaining a VAT number, choosing the KOR and claiming the startersaftrek, and with the first VAT return and first income tax return done together with the bookkeeper. The FAQ notes that entrepreneurs can join next to a job and that the first subscription covers a full fiscal year before monthly cancellation applies.
items.implication: Design onboarding as a guided first quarter — set-up checklist, first uploads coached, first VAT return explained — and measure time to first compliant filing per starter; a starter who reaches a clean first income tax return has learned the method and is the cheapest long-term client to keep.

items.title: A free intro call, a mutual-fit check and a no-external-software rule keep onboarding personal and the administration on one platform
items.summary: Kees describes its onboarding as a free introduction via Google Meet in which both sides check whether they fit, after which the client gets access to the app and a personal bookkeeper. Clients switching from a previous bookkeeper supply digital copies of earlier returns so the administration continues without gaps. The FAQ states that administrations kept in external accounting software are not accepted, that multiple trading names can be run in one administration, that the first subscription covers a full fiscal year, and that thereafter clients can cancel monthly with one calendar month's notice.
items.implication: The fit check is a deliberate filter: track intro-to-active conversion together with first-year retention so that sales does not win clients the bookkeepers cannot serve well; make the switch service (importing history, mapping old categories) a repeatable product because every switched client arrives with an administration that must be reconciled before the first VAT return.

items.title: Professional associations and service providers concentrate the creative freelancer audience and lower acquisition cost through member benefits
items.summary: The partners page lists referral partnerships with voordekunst, BNO, Insify, DuPho, Unfair, Kunstenbond, BrightPensioen and DAS, and with Stichting BOK, which has more than 2,300 members and whose members join without administration costs and with three months free; BrightPensioen members receive a €50 discount. The home page and testimonials feature creative clients — a furniture designer, a stylist, a make-up artist, an artist and a pair of bakers — as client stories.
items.implication: Run the partner programme as a measured channel: a benefit code per partner, referral tracking from landing page to active client, and partner reporting on activated members; extend the same mechanism to insurance, pension and legal partners so that Kees becomes the financial home of the freelancer rather than only the bookkeeper.

items.title: Founders extends the fixed-fee model to BVs, so the path from eenmanszaak to holding and werkmaatschappij stays on one platform
items.summary: Founders (Founders Finance B.V., founded 2018, same Amsterdam address as Kees) prices its service for companies at €1,750 per year for a holding BV and €2,450 per year for a werkmaatschappij, excluding VAT and invoiced monthly, covering the corporate tax return, the statutory annual accounts and the KVK filing. The Kees FAQ points BV clients to Founders and lists payroll at €17.50 per payslip per employee per month, which also covers a DGA salary.
items.implication: Model the legal-form transition as a stream: a knowledge freelancer whose profit or Wet DBA exposure makes a BV attractive should be able to move to Founders without a new onboarding, with the sole-proprietor history, bookkeeper relationship and app continuing; corporate tax and statutory accounts are the specialised engine that justifies the higher fee.

items.title: Software-only competitors serve hundreds of thousands of entrepreneurs at €3 to €41 per month and are adding AI and bookkeeper plans
items.summary: Moneybird states that more than 400,000 entrepreneurs use its software and prices its plans between €3 and €41 per month; e-Boekhouden.nl states that over 500,000 entrepreneurs have used its platform. Jortt promotes an AI-boekhoudbot and built-in income tax (IB) and corporate tax (VPB) returns, and Tellow offers a 'Compleet' plan that includes a personal bookkeeper next to its software plans. Kees' own proposition is the personal bookkeeper plus app at €70 per month.
items.implication: The price gap must be explained by outcomes the software cannot promise — filings done on time by a named person, tax advice included, no surprises — so the app must be at least as good as the software-only tools on capture and dashboard, while the personal bookkeeper, the review quality and proactive advice are marketed and measured as the difference.

items.title: VOF, partner-return and payroll add-ons let a client grow from one person to partners and employees without changing bookkeeper
items.summary: The FAQ prices a VOF at €1,140 per year for two partners plus €100 per additional partner, a partner's income tax return at €125 including VAT, and payroll at €17.50 per payslip per employee per month; all are invoiced monthly on top of or as part of the fixed subscription. For a VOF the bookkeeper prepares the shared administration, the profit split and each partner's income tax return.
items.implication: Keep one client file per entity with multiple people attached (partners, a fiscal partner, employees) so that adding a partner or a first employee is a plan change in billing rather than a new onboarding; profit-split accuracy and partner-return on-time rate are the quality metrics for partnerships.

items.title: A real-time dashboard of revenue, costs, profit and VAT per quarter turns the administration into a reservation and decision tool
items.summary: The dashboard page describes direct insight into revenue per quarter, cost categories, investments, profit and the VAT to pay or receive per quarter, updated in real time as bookings are submitted and available on web and mobile. It positions the dashboard as the place where the entrepreneur sees how the business is doing and what to reserve for tax.
items.implication: Extend the dashboard from what happened to what is owed: an income tax reservation estimate based on year-to-date profit and known deductions, and per-partner views for VOFs, would answer the 'what do I need to set aside' question before the bookkeeper is asked, reducing advice load and unexpected tax bills.

items.title: The bookkeeper is the human layer that answers questions all year and updates clients proactively — the relationship is the product software cannot copy
items.summary: Kees describes its bookkeepers as personal contacts who check the administration, file on time, answer questions by e-mail and phone throughout the year, update clients about changes and deadlines that affect them, and are backed up by colleagues when absent. The FAQ and content pages cover typical advice topics such as buying a house as a freelancer, entrepreneurship next to a job, deductions and the Wet DBA. Vortex's page highlights that loyal clients act as brand ambassadors.
items.implication: Protect advice consistency as the company scales: log every client question, route recurring ones into a shared knowledge base with reviewed answers, and measure advice response time and first-time-right filings per bookkeeper, so that a client's experience does not depend on which of a hundred colleagues picks up the phone.

items.title: Founders prices BV work per entity and per full financial year, which makes corporate clients a distinct cost base rather than a bigger eenmanszaak
items.summary: Founders (Founders Finance B.V., founded 2018, same Amsterdam address as Kees de Boekhouder) lists a holding BV at €1,750 and a werkmaatschappij at €2,450 per year, each invoiced monthly and each covering a full financial year, with the VOF package referred back to Kees de Boekhouder. A DGA with a holding and an operating company therefore pays for two entities, and corporate tax returns, statutory annual accounts and KVK filing sit with a separate team.
items.implication: Model BV clients as multi-entity accounts with their own filing calendar (VPB, statutory accounts, KVK deposit) and their own bookkeeper capacity, and make the eenmanszaak-to-BV transition a first-class flow so the client keeps one login and one relationship while the back office changes.

items.title: Partner benefits are concrete and reciprocal: members get discounts and free months, Kees gets a referral channel it can measure
items.summary: The partners page lists nine partners with specific member benefits: BrightPensioen gives Kees clients a €50 discount on enrolment, Stichting BOK (2,300+ members) waives administration costs and adds three months of free membership, and Insify and DAS are offered through the client's own bookkeeper. Professional associations BNO, DuPho and Kunstenbond and the platforms voordekunst and Unfair supply the community side of the programme.
items.implication: Treat each partnership as a two-way funnel with its own tracking (partner-referred intro calls, benefit uptake by Kees clients) rather than a logo wall, and give bookkeepers a scripted moment to surface insurance, pension and legal benefits so partners see measurable value back.

items.title: A VOF is priced and filed per partner, so partnerships are a per-head service on one shared administration
items.summary: The FAQ prices a VOF at €1,140 per year for two partners plus €100 for every additional partner, invoiced monthly, and lists the partner income tax return separately at €125 including VAT. One administration is shared, but the profit split and each partner's own income tax return are separate deliverables of the same bookkeeper.
items.implication: The VOF flow needs per-partner objects (share, deductions, hours criterion, own income tax return and deadline) on top of the shared ledger, and partner changes must update billing and the filing calendar together; bookkeeper capacity planning should count partners, not administrations.
